When multiple Notifications are simultaneously triggered for the same record and addressed to the same recipient(s), the Weight field value determines which notification(s) to send and which to skip. cad-udemy-176678835.gatilho: Why is important that Deny-Unless ACLs are evaluated before Allow-If ACLs?
cad-udemy-176678835.macete: Why is important that Deny-Unless ACLs are evaluated before Allow-If ACLs? → To restrict access by default and ensure security
cad-udemy-176678835.conexao:
O gabarito fornecido associa este cenário a: To restrict access by default and ensure security. Explicação do material: Deny-Unless ACL

Deny-Unless ACLs block access unless everything checks out. If they fail, no other rules are checked, and the user is denied access.

How Does It Work?

If the user meets all requirements (role, condition, and script), the ACL passes, and other rules (Allow-If ACLs) decide if access is allowed.

If any requirement fails, the ACL fails, and access is blocked immediately.

Which Comes First?

Deny-Unless ACLs are always checked before Allow-If ACLs. If the Deny-Unless fails, access is blocked—no further rules are checked.

>User doesn’t have the required role

Fail: Access is denied immediately.
User has the role but the record is inactive

Fail: One rule is not met, so access is blocked.

Reference: ServiceNow Deny-Unless ACL

The current object is a GlideRecord that contains the record as it exists in the buffer, including the changes made by the user on the form.

current.short_description = "Updated by BR: " + current.short_description;

The previous object is a read-only GlideRecord containing the values of the record exactly as they exist in the database before the current update.

if (current.assignment_group != previous.assignment_group) { // do something }

The GlideRecord API is the standard way to interact with the ServiceNow database. While current and previous are specific instances of a GlideRecord, you can also initialize new GlideRecord objects within your script to look up data in other tables.

Usage: Querying related records or performing validation against different tables.

cad-udemy-179081237.gatilho:
A custom table x_teddybear_project extends the Task table.
The following ACLs are configured:

Table ACL:

x_teddybear_project | read

Role required: itil

Field ACLs:

x_teddybear_project.field1 | read

No specific roles required (inherits table access)

x_teddybear_project.field2 | read

No field-level ACL defined

x_teddybear_project.field3 | read

Role required: admin

No other ACLs exist on this table or fields.

Which field or fields can a user with the itil role read?
cad-udemy-179081237.macete:
A custom table x_teddybear_project extends the Task table.
The following ACLs are configured:

Table ACL:

x_teddybear_project | read

Role required: itil

Field ACLs:

x_teddybear_project.field1 | read

No specific roles required (inherits table access)

x_teddybear_project.field2 | read

No field-level ACL defined

x_teddybear_project.field3 | read

Role required: admin

No other ACLs exist on this table or fields.

Which field or fields can a user with the itil role read? → All fields except field3
cad-udemy-179081237.conexao:
O gabarito fornecido associa este cenário a: All fields except field3. Explicação do material: The correct answer is All fields except field3.

To understand why, we have to look at how ServiceNow processes Access Control Lists (ACLs) using a "top-down" approach, moving from the general (table level) to the specific (field level).

The ACL Evaluation Process

In ServiceNow, for a user to see a field, they must pass two gates:

Gate 1 (Table Level): Does the user have permission to see the table?

Gate 2 (Field Level): Does the user have permission to see the specific field?

Breaking Down the Access for the ITIL User

Table Access: The user has the itil role. Since the Table ACL for x_teddybear_project requires the itil role, the user passes Gate 1. They can now access the records in the table.

field1 Access: There is a field-level ACL, but it doesn't list any specific roles. In ServiceNow, if a field ACL exists without specific roles, it essentially inherits the table-level requirement. Since the user passed the table-level check, they can read field1.

field2 Access: There is no field-level ACL defined at all. When no field-level ACL exists, the system defaults to the table-level result. Since the user is allowed to read the table, they are granted access to all fields on that table that don't have their own specific restrictions. Therefore, they can read field2.

field3 Access: There is a specific field-level ACL that requires the admin role. This is an "explicit" restriction. Even though the ITIL user passed the table-level check, they do not have the admin role required by this specific field-level gate. Therefore, they cannot read field3.

Reference: Configure security (ServiceNow Docs)

O gabarito fornecido associa este cenário a: b, c, and d. Explicação do material: In ServiceNow, Script Includes are used to store reusable server-side logic. The correct benefits of storing the majority of an application’s server-side logic in a Script Include are:

Only run when called from a script

Script Includes do not execute automatically. They run only when another script explicitly calls them, which improves control and avoids unnecessary execution.

The script logic can be hidden when the Application is installed from the ServiceNow Store

Script Includes can be marked as protected, preventing customers from viewing or modifying the code after installation. This is especially important for applications distributed through the ServiceNow Store.

Centralizing logic in a Script Include improves maintainability and reuse. When business logic changes, developers update it in one location instead of multiple scripts.

cad-udemy-179081227.gatilho: What functionality is supported by Flow Designer?

Modular Automation: Flow Designer explicitly supports the ability to call subflows. This allows developers to build reusable chunks of logic (e.g., "Create AD User" or "Send Slack Notification") that can be triggered by multiple parent flows.

cad-udemy-179081229.gatilho: What is a characteristic of Modules?

The Correct Answer: Every Module must be part of an Application Menu

Key Breakdown

cad-udemy-179081245.gatilho: In your data model, there is a relationship between the Assigned To user and their Manager. Breakdown Relations use this relationship that is current as of?
cad-udemy-179081245.macete: In your data model, there is a relationship between the Assigned To user and their Manager. Breakdown Relations use this relationship that is current as of? → When the Data Collector is executed.
cad-udemy-179081245.conexao:
O gabarito fornecido associa este cenário a: When the Data Collector is executed.. Explicação do material: Breakdown Relations and Data Collection

In Performance Analytics, Breakdown Relations allow you to navigate through hierarchical data (like an organizational structure) by defining a relationship between two breakdown elements (e.g., Assigned To and Manager).

The Correct Answer When the Data Collector is executed.

Key Breakdown

Snapshot in Time: Performance Analytics is designed to capture a "snapshot" of data. When the Data Collector job runs, it queries the current state of the records (including the Assigned To and their Manager) and stores that specific relationship in the scores table.

Point-of-Collection: If a user’s manager changes after the data collector has finished its run, that change will not be reflected in the existing scores for that day. The system uses the relationship that was active at the exact moment the data was "collected."

Consistency: This ensures that historical trending remains accurate to what the organizational structure actually looked like on the day the data was recorded.

Reference: View the data collection job logs (ServiceNow Docs)

cad-udemy-179081247.gatilho: When a user reports that they are not able to see modules on the application navigator, what can you do, to see what modules are visible to them?

O gabarito fornecido associa este cenário a: Impersonate the user. Explicação do material: User Impersonation

In ServiceNow, Impersonation is the standard administrative feature used to view the instance exactly as another user sees it. This is the most effective way to troubleshoot visibility issues, such as missing modules, hidden fields, or restricted records.

The Correct Answer: Impersonate the user

Key Breakdown

Validation: By impersonating the user, you can verify if their Roles or Access Control Lists (ACLs) are correctly allowing them to see specific Application Menus and Modules.

Security: This does not require knowing the user's password. It is a built-in platform capability granted to administrators (or those with the impersonator role).

Audit Trail: Every impersonation session is logged in the system (sys_user_logon) to ensure accountability.

Reference: Impersonate a user (ServiceNow Docs)

cad-udemy-179081249.gatilho: Which ServiceNow capability provides assistance to help other users obtain information, make decisions, and perform common work tasks via a messaging interface?
cad-udemy-179081249.macete: Which ServiceNow capability provides assistance to help other users obtain information, make decisions, and perform common work tasks via a messaging interface? → Virtual Agent
cad-udemy-179081249.conexao:
O gabarito fornecido associa este cenário a: Virtual Agent. Explicação do material: ServiceNow Virtual Agent

The Virtual Agent is a conversational platform that enables users to obtain information, make decisions, and perform common work tasks through a messaging interface. It serves as a 24/7 automated "first line of support" that can handle routine requests without human intervention.

The Correct Answer: Virtual Agent

Key Breakdown

Conversational Interface: It provides a chat-based experience (Natural Language Understanding/NLU) where users can type in plain language (e.g., "I need a new laptop" or "My VPN is down").

Decision Support: The bot can ask clarifying questions to help the user make a choice or troubleshoot an issue (e.g., "Is this for a Mac or PC?").

Task Automation: Unlike a simple FAQ bot, the Virtual Agent is integrated with Workflows and Flow Designer. It can actually do work, such as resetting a password, updating a record, or ordering an item from the Service Catalog.

Multi-Channel: It can be embedded in the Service Portal, Microsoft Teams, Slack, or ServiceNow’s mobile apps.

Reference: Overview tab (ServiceNow Docs)

cad-udemy-179081251.gatilho: Which feature allows you to automate business logic for a particular application or process such as approvals, tasks notifications, and record operations?
cad-udemy-179081251.macete: Which feature allows you to automate business logic for a particular application or process such as approvals, tasks notifications, and record operations? → Flows
cad-udemy-179081251.conexao:
O gabarito fornecido associa este cenário a: Flows. Explicação do material: In the ServiceNow Flow Designer, a Flow is the primary automated process used to execute business logic. It consists of a Trigger (which tells the flow when to start) and one or more Actions (which tell the flow what to do).

Automation Capabilities: Flows are designed to replace legacy tools like Workflow Editor for most use cases. They can handle approvals, send notifications, create or update records, and even integrate with external systems via IntegrationHub.

Low-Code/No-Code: The main benefit of Flows is that they allow process owners and developers to build complex logic using a natural language interface rather than writing complex JavaScript.

Reference: Flow Designer (ServiceNow Docs)

cad-udemy-179081253.gatilho: From a form, what would you click to add additional fields to the form? (Choose two.)
cad-udemy-179081253.macete: From a form, what would you click to add additional fields to the form? (Choose two.) → Context Menu > Configure > Form Layout + Context Menu > Configure > Form Design
cad-udemy-179081253.conexao:
O gabarito fornecido associa este cenário a: Context Menu > Configure > Form Layout; Context Menu > Configure > Form Design. Explicação do material: When you are viewing a record in ServiceNow and need to modify the UI (add, remove, or rearrange fields), you use the Context Menu (the three lines or "hamburger" icon in the header, or a right-click on the header).

Form Layout: This is the classic interface. It uses a "Slushbucket" (two columns) where you move fields from the "Available" side to the "Selected" side. It is very fast for simply adding existing fields or creating a few new ones quickly.

Form Design: This is the modern, drag-and-drop visual editor. It allows you to see a live representation of the form, organize fields into sections, and add new fields by dragging them from a sidebar. It is generally preferred for complex layouts.

Reference: Configuring the form layout (ServiceNow Docs)

cad-udemy-179081255.gatilho: What is the name of the table relationship, where two or more tables are related in a bi-directional relationship, so that the related records are visible from both tables in a related list?
cad-udemy-179081255.macete: What is the name of the table relationship, where two or more tables are related in a bi-directional relationship, so that the related records are visible from both tables in a related list? → Many to Many
cad-udemy-179081255.conexao:
O gabarito fornecido associa este cenário a: Many to Many. Explicação do material: In ServiceNow, a Many-to-Many (M2M) relationship allows multiple records in one table to be associated with multiple records in another table. This is achieved by using a "junction" or "intersection" table that sits between the two primary tables.

Bi-directional visibility: Because of the junction table, you can add a Related List to both tables. For example, in a relationship between Users and Groups, a User record shows all the Groups they belong to, and a Group record shows all the Users who are members.

The Junction Table: When you create a Many-to-Many relationship (via the sys_m2m table), ServiceNow automatically generates this third table to track the pairs of related sys_ids.

Reference: Create a many-to-many table relationship (ServiceNow Docs)

cad-udemy-179081257.gatilho: Group records are stored in which table?
cad-udemy-179081257.macete: Group records are stored in which table? → Group [sys_user_group]
cad-udemy-179081257.conexao:
O gabarito fornecido associa este cenário a: Group [sys_user_group]. Explicação do material: In ServiceNow, user groups are a fundamental part of the platform's security and task management architecture. They are stored in the sys_user_group table.

Table Naming Convention: In ServiceNow, "System" tables (core platform tables) almost always begin with the sys_ prefix. Because user and group management is a core platform function, the table name follows this standard.

Purpose of Groups: Groups are used to:

Assign Tasks: Tickets like Incidents or Changes are assigned to an "Assignment Group" (sys_user_group).

Grant Permissions: Roles are assigned to groups rather than individual users to simplify administration.

Subscription/Notifications: Groups can be added to a "Watch List" to receive collective updates.

Reference: Create a user group (ServiceNow Docs)

cad-udemy-179081231.gatilho: Which of the following are configured in an Email Notification? (Choose three.)
cad-udemy-179081231.macete: Which of the following are configured in an Email Notification? (Choose three.) → Who will receive the notification + What content will be in the notification + When to send the notification
cad-udemy-179081231.conexao:
O gabarito fornecido associa este cenário a: Who will receive the notification; What content will be in the notification; When to send the notification. Explicação do material: In ServiceNow, an Email Notification is configured using a specific record that defines the logic for outbound communication. These three components form the core tabs of the Notification configuration form.

When to send: This defines the "Trigger." It can be based on a specific event (like incident.inserted) or a change in a record's conditions (e.g., Priority changes to 1 - Critical).

Who will receive: This defines the "Audience." You can specify hard-coded users/groups, or use dynamic fields from the record, such as the Assigned to, Caller, or Watch list.

What it will contain: This defines the "Message." You can use Email Templates, hard-coded text, or HTML with dynamic variables (e.g., Short Description: ${short_description}) to personalize the email for the recipient.

Reference: Create an email notification (ServiceNow Docs)

cad-udemy-179081259.gatilho: What are the available Link types that can be assigned to a module in ServiceNow?
cad-udemy-179081259.macete: What are the available Link types that can be assigned to a module in ServiceNow? → Assessment, List of Records, Separator, Timeline Page
cad-udemy-179081259.conexao:
O gabarito fornecido associa este cenário a: Assessment, List of Records, Separator, Timeline Page. Explicação do material: In ServiceNow, Modules are the individual links within the Application Navigator (the left-hand sidebar). Each module is configured with a specific Link type that determines what happens when a user clicks on it—whether it opens a table, a dashboard, or a specialized interface.

The Correct Answer: Assessment, List of Records, Separator, Timeline Page

Key Breakdown:

Assessment: Opens a list of assessments or surveys assigned to the user.

List of Records: The most common type; it opens a filtered list of records for a specific table ("All Open Incidents").

Separator: This isn't a clickable link, but a label or a line used to visually group other modules within an application (the "Administration" header).

Timeline Page: Opens a timeline visualization, often used in Project Management or Change Management to see schedules.

Additional Common Link Types Include:

Run a Report: Directly opens a specific report.

New Record: Opens a blank form to create a new entry in a table.

URL (from arguments:) : Allows you to link to an external website or a specific page within ServiceNow using a relative URL.

Single Record: Opens one specific, pre-defined record.

Reference: Application Navigator category (ServiceNow Docs)
